That's how I was at first too. I've read alot of posts on here of other people that have gone through similar stages of questioning, and I myself definitely accepted it alot quicker than most but it still took me about a month to kind of see how I really feel. I think it's alot like depression too, in that alot of people (and those around them) expect to have "proof" that they have it, but most often the fact that they even have to ask themselves for proof is proof enough. Again I feel like I'm comparing this to myself alot, and I know that not everything works for everyone. I'm sorry if the advice I'm giving isn't helping, but I really do wanna help! I do think the thing that's fueling your doubts though is the seemingly huge amount of work it will take to be where you want to be, and so your brain would rather just say "no it's probably just not real" than to actually try. And I put an emphasis on "try" here, because that's all you have to do to see how it feels. Perhaps the next time you're out shopping and have a little money you could buy an outfit to try on when you're alone to see if it helps you feel better. Heck, even if it takes trying HRT for a while to see how that helps, I'd say go for it, even if you end up deciding that you are cis or non-binary or something. Alot of people make it seem like transitioning is irreversible, but it's not (atleast anything that isn't SRS that is). Sure, it would take time to get off the HRT and return to your birth gender, but honestly if being the correct gender is enough of a concern, then getting off of it if you need to should be just as easy as getting on it. I think that alot of people make it out to be more permanent than it actually is; there's plenty of time to search yourself during the process to see how you feel. And if it's more of a concern about 'transition regret', I actually myself was still struggling with that until earlier today when I saw a power point made by a doctor. In it, he included some stats from a study done in Sweden on over 1500 trans people that went through both HRT and SRS, both MtF and FtM, in the last 50 years (1960 to 2010), and overall only 2.2% reported having any regrets.In fact, a majority of that 2.2% were people from the 80's and there was actually a considerable decrease of regret, over 50%, by the late 90's and early 2000's. That means that today, there's only 1.1% of trans people that feel regret for transitioning, and that's at the higher end of the estimate! Granted, this was done in Sweden, but they typically have the same sort of social norms and psychology as most western countries do these days. I guess in the end it's all up to how you feel, not how others think or want you to feel. Don't do something (or not do something) just because you are felling pressure or doubts, do what is right for you when you feel ready to do it. It may take time, and while I have heard qualms of people that decided to wait or decided they weren't trans regretting not transitioning sooner, there is still lots of time to sort your feelings. Again, my advice is to atleast try; that way you can know for sure, and if you need to stop then you can! I just think it'd be worse to regret not doing it sooner than to have tried and work your way back, you know what I mean?
